opts.label: Compare groups (is A different from B?)
Design an experiment / how many units?
Predict an outcome for each customer/account
Measure the causal impact of an action
Choose an evaluation metric or threshold
Monitor a model or KPI over time

N-DESC-Q1.q: First — has the data been profiled and quality-checked?

opts.label: Yes — values are missing and I need to decide what to do
Profiling flagged duplicates, impossible values or unit errors
I worry the data only contains survivors / approved cases

N-DESC-Q2.q: What does the distribution look like (histogram / ECDF)?

opts.label: A few values look impossible or extreme

N-DESC-Q3.q: What types are the two variables?

opts.label: The relationship flips when I split by a third variable

N-DESC-PROFILE.use: Always first. Types, nulls, uniques, ranges, duplicates, impossible values, grain.
check: Business rules (no negative prices; returns flagged)
fail: Write a rule per issue and count rows affected before changing anything
N-DESC-PROFILE.act: Fix at source where possible; document every rule in the analysis log.
scenarios: S44 Claude Code reports a number you cannot reproduce

N-DESC-QUALITY.use: Profiling flagged duplicates, impossible values or unit errors.
check: Is the value impossible or merely unusual?
fail: Quarantine doubtful rows into a separate file rather than deleting
N-DESC-QUALITY.act: Correct, quarantine or keep with a flag — never silently drop.

N-DESC-SYM.use: Symmetric numeric data without heavy tails.
alt: Coefficient of variation to compare spread across scales
pit: Reporting mean of a skewed variable as "typical"
N-DESC-SYM.act: Use the mean for planning totals; quote SD for variability.

N-DESC-SKEW.t: Median, IQR, percentiles (P90/P99), MAD; log-scale histogram, ECDF; Lorenz/Pareto
N-DESC-SKEW.use: Spend, income, balances, claim amounts — skewed or heavy-tailed.
fail: keep the mean but show the tail separately
pit: Averages driven by a few bulk buyers
N-DESC-SKEW.act: Describe the typical customer with the median; manage the tail as its own segment.
scenarios: S03 Average basket jumped because of a few bulk buyers

N-DESC-OUTLIER.t: Outlier scan — IQR fences, robust (MAD) z-score; decide keep / cap / exclude / model separately
N-DESC-OUTLIER.use: Values far from the rest; suspected errors.
check: Effect on key results with and without
fail: Use robust statistics instead of deleting
pit: Using a plain z-score on skewed data
N-DESC-OUTLIER.act: Correct errors; keep genuine extremes but report sensitivity.
scenarios: S03 Average basket jumped because of a few bulk buyers

N-DESC-MISSING.t: Missing-data diagnosis (MCAR / MAR / MNAR) and treatment
N-DESC-MISSING.use: Any variable with missing values that matters to the analysis.
check: Do rows with missing values differ in outcome (MNAR?)
fail: MNAR → keep a "missing" category / flag and run a sensitivity analysis
alt: Simple imputation only for MCAR and small rates
pit: Listwise deletion that silently removes risky customers
N-DESC-MISSING.act: Document mechanism, method and rows affected; never hide missingness.
scenarios: S33 Income is missing more often for risky applicants

N-DESC-CORR.t: Scatter plot first, then Pearson (linear) / Spearman (monotone) / Kendall (small n, ties)
fail: Non-linear → Spearman or binned means; outliers → robust or rank methods
N-DESC-CORR.act: Use as a lead for further analysis, not a decision.

N-DESC-XTAB.t: Contingency table with row/column % and Cramér's V
alt: Chi-square test (→ T-TEST) if inference is needed
N-DESC-XTAB.act: Show the comparison that matches the decision.

N-DESC-STRATIFY.t: Stratified analysis — check for Simpson's paradox and confounding
N-DESC-STRATIFY.use: An overall comparison may be distorted by a third variable (format, channel, vintage).
check: Is the third variable related to both groups and outcome?
fail: Report within-stratum results and a weighted overall
alt: Regression with the confounder as a covariate (→ T-REG)
N-DESC-STRATIFY.act: Decide on the within-stratum result; explain the reversal.
scenarios: S02 Promotion looks harmful overall but helpful in every store format
S23 Is the default rate different for unverified-income customers?

N-DESC-BIAS.use: The data only contains "survivors" (current SKUs, approved applicants, active customers).
check: What is missing from the population?
fail: declined applications) or state the limitation
N-DESC-BIAS.act: Restate conclusions for the population actually analysed.
scenarios: S19 'Delisted SKUs never mattered' analysis

N-DIST-Q1.q: What kind of quantity is it?

opts.label: Count of events in a period (units sold, claims)
Positive skewed amount (spend, income, claim size)
Sample drawn without replacement from a small lot (audit)

N-DIST-Q2.q: Compare the variance with the mean.

N-DIST-BIN.t: Bernoulli / Binomial (Beta-Binomial if the rate varies across groups)
N-DIST-BIN.use: Defaults in a vintage, conversions in an A/B test.
fail: Rate varies by store/branch → Beta-Binomial or hierarchical model
alt: Logistic regression to model the rate
N-DIST-BIN.act: Quote the rate with its interval.

N-DIST-POIS.use: Counts with variance ≈ mean (claims per policy, baskets per hour).
fail: Over-dispersion → Negative Binomial; varying exposure → rate with offset
pit: Assuming Poisson for retail SKU sales (usually over-dispersed)
N-DIST-POIS.act: Use for capacity and frequency planning.

N-DIST-NB.use: Over-dispersed counts (weekly SKU units, claims with heterogeneous risk).
pit: Under-stated uncertainty if Poisson is used
N-DIST-NB.act: Size safety stock with the wider spread.

N-DIST-AMT.t: Lognormal or Gamma (compare Q-Q plots and AIC)
fail: Extreme tail → separate large-loss model / Pareto tail
N-DIST-AMT.act: Use quantiles (P90, P99) for limits and reserves.

N-DIST-TIME.t: Exponential (constant hazard) → Weibull (changing hazard); censoring-aware methods
N-DIST-TIME.use: Time to churn, time to default, time between purchases.
pit: Averaging only observed event times (ignores censoring)
N-DIST-TIME.act: Use survival curves for retention planning.
scenarios: S37 When do customers churn?

N-DIST-BETA.use: Prior/posterior for a conversion or default rate.
pit: Treating a small-sample rate as exact
N-DIST-BETA.act: Report probability that rate exceeds a threshold.

N-DIST-HYPER.use: Audit samples drawn without replacement from a finite file population.
check: Sample is a large share of the lot
fail: Small share → Binomial approximation is fine
pit: Using Binomial when sampling 50 of 200 files
N-DIST-HYPER.act: Choose sample size for a target detection probability.
scenarios: S42 Is an audit sample of 50 files enough?

N-TEST-Q0.q: Is this an experiment that needs an SRM / design check first?

opts.label: Yes — randomised test, not yet checked
I am running many tests at once

N-TEST-Q2.q: How many groups, and are they independent?

opts.label: 2 groups and I have a strong pre-period measure per unit
Very small samples; I want minimal assumptions
I need to adjust for several covariates

N-TEST-Q3.q: How many groups / is it paired?

N-TEST-2G-MEAN.t: Welch two-sample t-test (+ effect size and CI)
N-TEST-2G-MEAN.use: Compare average outcome between two independent groups — at the unit that was randomised.
check: Independent units (aggregate to store/branch if randomised there)
fail: Heavy tails and small n → Mann-Whitney or bootstrap CI
Clustered rows → aggregate to cluster or mixed model
Size differences → growth vs own pre-period
pit: Testing transaction lines when stores were randomised
N-TEST-2G-MEAN.act: Roll out / extend / stop — sized by the CI of the lift, not the p-value.
scenarios: S01 Did the store-level Hair Care feature promotion lift sales?

N-TEST-2G-PROP.t: Two-proportion z-test (Fisher's exact if any expected cell < 5)
N-TEST-2G-PROP.use: Compare a rate (default, conversion, cure) between two independent groups.
pit: Base-rate blindness (0.5 pp may be huge at a 4% base)
N-TEST-2G-PROP.act: Quote risk difference in pp and relative risk; translate to accounts or units per 1,000.
scenarios: S23 Is the default rate different for unverified-income customers?
S38 Champion vs challenger collections strategy

N-TEST-PAIRED.t: Paired t-test (Wilcoxon signed-rank if differences are skewed)
N-TEST-PAIRED.use: Same units measured twice (store before/after, customer pre/post).
alt: Difference-in-differences when a control group exists (→ T-CAUSAL)
N-TEST-PAIRED.act: Use only with a control group for causal claims.

N-TEST-KG.t: One-way ANOVA (+ Levene); Welch ANOVA + Games-Howell if variances differ; Kruskal-Wallis + Dunn if non-normal
N-TEST-KG.act: Act on the pairs that differ by a meaningful amount.
scenarios: S04 Which of four regions has a different basket value?

N-TEST-CHI.t: Chi-square test of independence (Fisher exact for small tables) + Cramér's V
pit: Huge n makes trivial associations significant
N-TEST-CHI.act: Report the effect size, not just p.
scenarios: S05 Is promo uptake independent of loyalty tier?

N-TEST-COUNT.t: Poisson / Negative Binomial rate comparison (GLM with exposure offset)
N-TEST-COUNT.use: Claims per policy-year, units per store-week.

N-TEST-SURV.t: Kaplan-Meier curves + log-rank test (RMST if hazards cross)
N-TEST-SURV.use: Time to churn or default with censoring.
fail: Crossing curves → restricted mean survival time
pit: Comparing average time among churners only
scenarios: S37 When do customers churn?

N-TEST-MULTI.t: Multiple-testing correction — Holm (family-wise) or Benjamini-Hochberg (false discovery rate)
N-TEST-MULTI.use: Many segments, metrics or features tested.
check: How many tests were run (including ones not reported)?
fail: Pre-register primary metric; treat the rest as exploratory
N-TEST-MULTI.act: Re-test winners on fresh data before acting.
scenarios: S43 A junior ran 40 segment tests and found 3 'wins'

N-TEST-PERM.use: Small samples or unusual statistics; minimal assumptions.
pit: Permuting at the wrong level (lines vs stores)
N-TEST-PERM.act: Use alongside the main test as a robustness check.

N-EXP-Q1.q: Can you randomise who/what gets the treatment?

opts.label: Yes — I need a sample size
Yes — the test is running/finished and I need to check it
Yes — variance is high and the test would take too long
Yes — stakeholders want to look at results early
Yes — I want the probability B beats A

N-EXP-POWER.t: Power and sample size (α, power, MDE, baseline variance; cluster design effect)
N-EXP-POWER.use: Before any test — how many customers/stores/weeks?
pit: Forgetting the design effect for store-level tests
N-EXP-POWER.act: Agree MDE and duration with the business before launch.
scenarios: S21 How many stores for the next promo test?

fail: find the assignment or logging bug; do not trust the results
pit: Analysing a broken test because "the lift looks good"
scenarios: S01 Did the store-level Hair Care feature promotion lift sales?
S38 Champion vs challenger collections strategy

N-EXP-CUPED.use: High-variance metrics with a correlated pre-period measure.
pit: Using covariates affected by the treatment
N-EXP-CUPED.act: Shorter tests with the same power.
scenarios: S21 How many stores for the next promo test?

N-EXP-SEQ.use: Need to monitor results before the planned end.
check: Planned looks and boundaries defined upfront
fail: Ad-hoc peeking → treat results as exploratory
alt: Bayesian monitoring with pre-agreed decision rule
scenarios: S22 Daily dashboard: did this week's dip matter?

N-BAYES-AB.t: Bayesian A/B test (Beta-Binomial; P(B > A), expected loss)
N-BAYES-AB.use: Decision-makers want probability statements; prior knowledge exists.
fail: Sensitive to prior → report with a weak prior too
N-BAYES-AB.act: Ship when expected loss is below an agreed tolerance.

opts.label: Elasticity: % change in units for % change in price
Many predictors / signs flip / VIF high
Risk jumps above a threshold (curved effect)

N-REG-OLS.use: Explain a continuous outcome with several drivers.
fail: Heteroscedastic → robust SEs or log outcome; outliers → robust/quantile regression; collinear → Ridge
N-REG-OLS.act: Use coefficients as "all else equal" associations; test causality separately.

fail: Non-linear → bins/WoE or splines; rare events → penalised (Firth)
pit: Interpreting odds ratios as risk ratios when the outcome is common
N-REG-LOGIT.act: Score, rank, and set cut-offs with business costs.

N-REG-GLM.t: GLM — Poisson/Negative Binomial for counts (offset for exposure), Gamma for positive amounts, Tweedie for zero + positive
N-REG-GLM.use: Counts, claim severity, spend including non-buyers.
fail: Over-dispersion → NB; many zeros → zero-inflated/hurdle or Tweedie
N-REG-GLM.act: Price and plan on predicted means and quantiles.

N-REG-LOGLOG.t: Log-log regression / Poisson GLM on log price (elasticity), with promo, display, SKU, store and week controls
check: Price variation not driven only by promotions
fail: No exogenous price variation → run a price test
pit: Using chain-level averages that mix stores
scenarios: S07 How price-sensitive is the Snacks category?

N-REG-VIF.t: Multicollinearity check (VIF) → drop/combine features or regularise (Ridge, Lasso, Elastic Net)
N-REG-VIF.use: Correlated predictors; unstable or flipping coefficient signs.
pit: Dropping the variable the business cares about without explanation
N-REG-VIF.act: Explain combined drivers, not individual unstable coefficients.
scenarios: S35 Income and limit both in the model; signs flip

N-REG-INTERACT.t: Interaction terms, splines/polynomials; mixed models for grouped data
N-REG-INTERACT.use: Effect depends on a second variable (young × high DTI) or is curved (utilisation).
pit: Interpreting main effects alone when interaction is present
N-REG-INTERACT.act: Target policies at the combination, not each factor alone.
scenarios: S34 Risk jumps above 80% utilisation; young customers with high DTI look worse

pit: A single linear term hides the threshold
N-REG-NONLINEAR.act: Set policy rules at the threshold.
scenarios: S34 Risk jumps above 80% utilisation; young customers with high DTI look worse

N-REG-ANCOVA.t: Regression of outcome on group + pre-period covariate (ANCOVA / CUPED-style)
N-REG-ANCOVA.use: Two-group comparison with a strong baseline covariate.
N-REG-ANCOVA.act: Tighter CI for the same data.

N-REG-GLM-INS.t: Frequency-severity GLMs (Poisson/NB × Gamma) or Tweedie pure premium
scenarios: S40 Claims frequency and severity pricing

opts.label: Regulator/customer needs reasons for each decision
Score looks too good to be true

N-ML-SCORECARD.t: Logistic scorecard with WoE binning (points to double the odds)
N-ML-SCORECARD.use: Credit decisions needing adverse-action reasons and stability.
fail: Weak lift → GBM challenger with SHAP under model-risk governance
N-ML-SCORECARD.act: Set cut-offs on profit/loss by score band.
scenarios: S24 Build an application scorecard

N-ML-GBM.t: Gradient boosting (LightGBM/XGBoost) vs logistic/linear baseline; random forest check
N-ML-GBM.act: Deploy with monitoring and a champion/challenger test.
scenarios: S25 Gradient boosting beats the scorecard by 3 Gini points

N-ML-IMBALANCE.t: Class weights or threshold moving (SMOTE with care); evaluate with PR-AUC, precision@k
N-ML-IMBALANCE.use: Rare events — fraud, default in good books.
alt: Anomaly detection for unseen patterns (→ T-ANOM)
N-ML-IMBALANCE.act: Set the threshold by cost or capacity (→ T-METRIC).
scenarios: S27 Fraud is 0.7% and the model is '99% accurate'

N-ML-LEAK.t: Leakage audit — target, temporal and preprocessing leakage
N-ML-LEAK.use: AUC suspiciously high (e.g. > 0.95 in credit), or a feature "too predictive".
check: Was preprocessing fit on all data?
Same customer in train and test?
fail: Remove post-outcome fields; refit pipeline inside CV
N-ML-LEAK.act: Never ship until the leak is explained.
scenarios: S26 Model AUC is 0.98 on day one

N-ML-DL.t: Deep learning (awareness) — usually not better than GBM on tabular data
N-ML-DL.act: Benchmark against a simple baseline first.

N-CLUST-Q1.q: What do the data and goal look like?

opts.label: Business rules are enough (recency, frequency, value)

scenarios: S14 Segment loyalty customers for CRM

N-CLUST-KMEANS.t: K-Means (scale features; choose k with elbow + silhouette; check stability)
pit: Clusters that do not change any action
N-CLUST-KMEANS.act: Name each cluster and link it to a different action.
scenarios: S14 Segment loyalty customers for CRM

N-CLUST-DBSCAN.act: Treat noise points as candidates for review.

N-SEG-BASKET.act: Bundle or co-locate high-lift, decent-support pairs.
scenarios: S15 What sells with what?

N-ANOM-Q1.q: What does the suspicious pattern look like?

opts.label: Amounts bunched just below a threshold
Numbers look made up or rounded

N-ANOM-MULTI.use: Multivariate outliers without labels (returns abuse, unusual accounts).
N-ANOM-MULTI.act: Route top alerts to investigators; measure precision.
scenarios: S16 A group of customers returns 40% of what they buy

N-ANOM-GRAPH.t: Graph / link analysis (connected components on shared devices and addresses)
N-ANOM-GRAPH.act: Investigate components above a size threshold.
scenarios: S29 Accounts share devices and addresses

N-ANOM-STRUCT.use: Deposits just below a reporting limit.
scenarios: S30 Cash deposits cluster just under the reporting limit

N-ANOM-BENFORD.t: Benford first-digit test + last-digit/rounding test, compared with peers
N-ANOM-BENFORD.use: Suspected fabricated figures (a store, branch, expense claims).
check: Data spans several orders of magnitude
Compare with peer units not only theory
fail: Narrow-range data → use peer comparison and rounding tests
pit: Treating a Benford deviation as proof
scenarios: S17 One store's numbers look too neat

N-FCST-Q1.q: What does the series look like?

N-FCST-SEASON.t: Decompose (STL) → ETS / SARIMA vs seasonal-naive baseline
fail: Does not beat baseline → use baseline
scenarios: S09 Forecast weekly category sales for the next 13 weeks

N-FCST-DRIVERS.t: ARIMAX / regression with lags / GBM with calendar and driver features
check: Driver values known at forecast time
pit: Using actual future weather/promos that will not be known

N-FCST-INTERMITTENT.t: Croston / SBA; classify with ADI and CV²; evaluate with MASE
N-FCST-INTERMITTENT.act: Stock policy by service level, not point forecast.
scenarios: S10 Long-tail SKUs sell zero most weeks

N-FCST-HIER.use: Forecasts needed at several levels that must add up.

N-FCST-BREAK.t: Change-point detection (CUSUM, PELT) then refit post-break
N-FCST-BREAK.use: Store refit, competitor opening, policy change.
scenarios: S11 One store's sales stepped down mid-year
S22 Daily dashboard: did this week's dip matter?

N-FCST-CENSOR.t: Treat stockout periods as censored demand before modelling
N-FCST-CENSOR.use: Sales understate demand when out of stock.
pit: Forecasting sales instead of demand → chronic under-stocking
scenarios: S12 Lost sales during stockouts

opts.label: Not random — first draw the causal diagram
Treated vs control, before and after

N-CAUSAL-DAG.t: Causal diagram (DAG) — adjust for confounders, not colliders or mediators
fail: Unmeasured confounders → sensitivity analysis or design an experiment
N-CAUSAL-DAG.act: Decide what can and cannot be claimed.
scenarios: S06 Display and promotion always run together — what drove sales?
S18 Loyalty members spend more — is the programme causing it?

N-CAUSAL-DID.use: Policy/promo applied to some stores or regions from a date.

N-CAUSAL-PSM.t: Propensity score matching / weighting (+ overlap and sensitivity checks)
N-CAUSAL-PSM.use: Loyalty membership, credit-limit increases chosen by the business.
N-CAUSAL-PSM.act: Present as best estimate with caveats.
scenarios: S18 Loyalty members spend more — is the programme causing it?

N-CAUSAL-UPLIFT.use: Target customers who change behaviour because of the treatment.

N-METRIC-Q1.q: What will the model output be used for?

N-METRIC-CLASS.t: ROC-AUC / Gini, KS, lift and gain by decile
N-METRIC-CLASS.act: Rule of thumb: application scorecards often AUC 0.70–0.85 (varies by product and regulator).
scenarios: S24 Build an application scorecard

N-METRIC-RARE.t: PR-AUC, precision@k, recall at investigator capacity
N-METRIC-RARE.act: Size the alert queue to capacity.
scenarios: S27 Fraud is 0.7% and the model is '99% accurate'

N-METRIC-CALIB.act: Recalibrate before using probabilities in money calculations.
scenarios: S24 Build an application scorecard

N-METRIC-COST.t: Expected-cost threshold (cost FN × FN + cost FP × FP) or capacity-based cut-off
N-METRIC-COST.use: Any yes/no decision from a score.
fail: Unknown costs → show the trade-off curve
N-METRIC-COST.act: Pick the threshold with the lowest expected cost.
scenarios: S28 Where to set the fraud alert threshold?

check: Level at which decisions are made
fail: Near-zero actuals → avoid MAPE; use WAPE/MASE
N-METRIC-REG.act: Report accuracy and bias at the decision level.
scenarios: S09 Forecast weekly category sales for the next 13 weeks

N-MON-Q1.q: What changed, or what are you worried about?

N-MON-PSI.use: Monthly model monitoring; data pipeline changes.
check: Rule of thumb: < 0.10 stable · 0.10–0.25 investigate · > 0.25 significant shift
pit: Treating PSI as a performance measure
scenarios: S31 The latest vintage defaults more

N-MON-CONCEPT.t: Performance decay by vintage (AUC/KS, calibration) — concept drift
N-MON-CONCEPT.use: Relationship between inputs and outcome changes.
scenarios: S31 The latest vintage defaults more
S32 PSI is stable but AUC dropped

N-MON-FAIR.t: Fairness metrics (approval rate ratio / 80% rule, equal opportunity) incl. proxy checks
pit: Assuming removing the protected attribute removes bias
scenarios: S25 Gradient boosting beats the scorecard by 3 Gini points
S36 Approval rates differ by group; region looks innocent

N-MON-REJECT.use: Models trained only on approved applicants.
check: Score distribution of declined vs booked
fail: or a small randomised approval test

N-OPT-PROMO.t: Promo uplift net of cannibalisation, halo and pull-forward → promo ROI
N-OPT-PROMO.act: Keep promotions with positive incremental margin.
scenarios: S08 Promo on the 400 ml shampoo; the 200 ml fell

N-OPT-INVENTORY.t: Safety stock = z(service level) × σ(demand over lead time); newsvendor for perishables; ABC/XYZ
N-OPT-INVENTORY.act: Set service levels by ABC/XYZ class.
scenarios: S12 Lost sales during stockouts
S13 Which SKUs deserve deeper stock?

N-OPT-MC.t: Monte Carlo simulation of the decision's P&L
N-OPT-MC.act: Choose the option with acceptable downside.
scenarios: S20 How to split marketing budget across media
S39 Expected loss for a portfolio
S41 1-day 99% VaR for a card book
